About Us Team Contact Scientific Resources Fellows Current Fellows Fellows by Year Fellows by Industry News Engage Our Program Eligibility and Selection Criteria How to Apply About Us Team Contact Scientific Resources Fellows Current Fellows Fellows by Year Fellows by Industry News Engage Our Program Eligibility and Selection Criteria How to Apply About Cyclotron Road Developing Entrepreneurial Science Cyclotron Road empowers entrepreneurial scientists to advance their ideas from concept to viable first product, positioning them for broad societal impact in the long term. Nestled within Berkeley Lab, Cyclotron Road is named for the Lab’s primary address, 1 Cyclotron Road. Like Sand Hill Road in Silicon Valley, notable for its high concentration of venture capitalist firms who provide funding for new companies, Cyclotron Road aims to provide funding and support to new scientific technologies, and facilitate bringing them to market. Recruits Founders Our program offers fellowships to innovators who are determined to drive their research projects to the market’s doorstep. The program allows them to advance their projects with the potential for global impact in fields such as energy, agriculture, and manufacturing. Empowers Innovation Our program offers entrepreneurs the
They gain access to world-class research facilities and expertise as well as training, mentorship, and networking programs tailored to their needs.

Department of Energy’s (DOE) Office of Technology Commercialization’s (OTC) Lab-Embedded Entrepreneurship Program (LEEP) provides innovators with early-stage energy startups and/or emerging technologies a two-year funded fellowship in one of four National Laboratories (“nodes”), supporting them as they develop and transition their ideas into the market.
Cyclotron Road LEEP was the first node to establish an entrepreneurial fellowship at a National Lab.

About Us Team Contact Scientific Resources Fellows Current Fellows Fellows by Year Fellows by Industry News Engage Our Program Eligibility and Selection Criteria How to Apply About Us Team Contact Scientific Resources Fellows Current Fellows Fellows by Year Fellows by Industry News Engage Our Program Eligibility and Selection Criteria How to Apply Eligibility and Selection Criteria Research Experience A bachelor’s degree and four or more years of post-baccalaureate scientific research, engineering, or technology development experience. Project/Company Lead Leading a technical project or company relevant to our target industries and based in the physical or biological sciences or related engineering disciplines. First-time Entrepreneur Leading the commercial development of a hardware-based technology innovation for the first time i.e., not a repeat hard-tech founder. Co-applicants are welcome. Development Potential A project or company must be in development and not yet ready for full-scale product sales at the time of the application deadline. Funding Limits Must not have raised more than $2,000,000 in debt or equity funding from non-governmental sources for the proposed project at the time of the application deadline. A Work Authorization Must
A Work Authorization Must be able to work in the U.S. for the duration of the fellowship and qualify for access to Berkeley Lab.
Potential For Impact A project with potential for impact in one or more key industry areas in alignment with the mission of the fellowship.
A Strong Case A strong case for why you and your project benefit from the fellowship and access to Berkeley Lab.

However, non-US citizens who are citizens of—or were born in—Iran, North Korea, Cuba, or Syria need U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) permission to work at Berkeley Lab. Participants affiliated with restricted entities and other countries of concern such as Belarus, the Russian Federation, and Ukraine (DNR, LNR and Crimea Regions) are also subject to additional review and approval. About Us Team Contact Scientific Resources Fellows Current Fellows Fellows by Year Fellows by Industry News Engage Our Program Eligibility and Selection Criteria How to Apply About Us Team Contact Scientific Resources Fellows Current Fellows Fellows by Year Fellows by Industry News Engage Our Program Eligibility and Selection Criteria How to Apply Our Program Empowering Tomorrow's Technology Leaders Cyclotron Road, the first node of the DOE’s Office of Technology Commercialization (OTC)’s Lab-Embedded Entrepreneurship Program (LEEP), supports leading entrepreneurial scientists as they advance technology projects with the potential for global impact. The program features a fellowship, located at Berkeley Lab, that supports these innovators, in partnership with the non-profit Activate, on their journey toward the development of commercially viable technology products. Fellows receive a living stipend, entrepreneurial training, and access to Berkeley Lab’s expertise and facilities. Two Years of Funding Fellows receive a yearly living stipend of $115,000, health insurance, a relocation stipend, and a travel allowance. This enables them to focus on their project full-time. Each project also receives $100,000 to $150,000 of research support at Berkeley Lab. World-class
Our program manages flexible lab space to complement the resources available through collaborators and User Facilities.
Fellows fully own or jointly own all intellectual property developed during their two-year fellowship term.
Our team works closely with fellows for networking opportunities, support, and mentorship.

Networking and Mentorship Our team meets with fellows one-on-one regularly to help develop priorities, provide guidance, and make connections to our broader network of advisors, industry experts, and investors.

We also facilitate connections between fellows and our broad network of Lab researchers, industry executives, investors, entrepreneurs, philanthropists, and other experts from academia, industry, government, and finance—any of whom can serve as advisors or partners.

Scientists and engineers from diverse disciplines including energy, biosciences, and robotics were encouraged to explore this unique opportunity to validate, scale, and fund their ideas from prototype to production. Entering its 10th year, the Cyclotron Road program at Lawrence Berkeley National Lab (Berkeley Lab) was the first of four LEEPs across the U.S. Since the program’s inception, startups founded by participants have secured more than $1.9 billion in follow-on funding.
